articles.translated_content:
Forbidden Solitaire 如何将纸牌游戏带到前沿

设计
访谈

Forbidden Solitaire 如何将纸牌游戏带到前沿

它的成功使Grey Alien Games能够接触到比以往更多的Steam玩家。

Khee Hoon Chan，撰稿人
2026年8月17日
8分钟阅读

图片来源：Gray Alien Games/Night Signal Entertainment

Microsoft Solitaire 作为各地无聊办公室职员的慰藉，其受欢迎程度不容低估。自1990年Windows 3.0起，这款游戏就预装在Windows系统中，此后便成为纸牌游戏类型的代名词，纸牌游戏是一个包含多种变体的卡牌游戏家族。具体来说，Microsoft Solitaire 基于一种名为Klondike的版本。

乍一看，纸牌游戏似乎并不是那种对普通Steam用户特别有吸引力的卡牌游戏。它通常是一种冥想般的消遣，这一类型更适合免费休闲游戏市场，而非Steam商店。

然而，Forbidden Solitaire 凭借其诱人的90年代模拟恐怖风格，成功吸引了这些玩家的目光。该游戏自4月发布以来，一度达到880名同时在线玩家。相比之下，开发商Grey Alien Games的其他纸牌游戏，如Regency Solitaire II和Shadowhand Solitaire，在Steam上的峰值同时在线人数分别仅为98人和20人。此外，Forbidden Solitaire 的商业成功——游戏在48小时内售出10,000份——意味着Grey Alien Games及其联合开发商Night Signal Entertainment能够在游戏发布后不久就开始考虑续作。

“我们花了一段时间才适应这款游戏的成功程度，因为我们不习惯游戏发布后表现如此出色。”开发者Jake Birkett表示，“但它来得正是时候，因为我们确实付出了努力。”

相关阅读：一次一页，突破模拟城市的极限

纸牌游戏已经成为Grey Alien Games的专长领域，尽管Birkett指出这并非他们涉足的唯一游戏类型。“顺便提一下，[Forbidden Solitaire] 是我们的第十七款游戏。”他说道，“我们还制作了16款其他游戏，[包括]七款三消游戏、七款纸牌游戏、一款城市建造游戏[以及其他一些作品]。”尽管如此，该工作室对纸牌游戏的钟爱显而易见；这是他们擅长的游戏类型。

大多数纸牌游戏都是免费休闲体验，其中大部分只是对这一类型的直接诠释。玩家通过重复的回合清除一摞摞卡牌。然而，Grey Alien Games的游戏并非如此；他们的作品通常包含你乍看之下可能意想不到的机制变体或巧思。以Fairway Solitaire为例，这是Birkett在2007年以承包商身份为Big Fish Games开发的一款游戏，Kotaku将其描述为“不仅仅是另一款无聊的iPhone免费纸牌游戏”；其纸牌玩法深深植根于高尔夫机制。与此同时，Eurogamer称赞Regency Solitaire是“对简·奥斯汀小说的俏皮而精准的模仿之作”。

相关阅读：Silent Hill: Townfall 如何深入探索主角的内心世界

此外，Birkett本人对纸牌游戏类型也情有独钟，他在1995年制作了自己的第一款纸牌游戏。在一家电脑店工作期间，他迷上了Microsoft Solitaire，只要不是在组装电脑，他就在玩这款游戏。随后，他在自己的Commodore Amiga上制作了一个游戏版本，甚至将其寄给一家出版社，希望它能够被收录在当时随游戏杂志附赠的演示光盘中。不幸的是，他从未收到回复，不过这并没有浇灭他对游戏开发的热情。

Birkett决定在2005年辞去商业软件开发方面的稳定工作，创立Grey Alien Games。随后，他的妻子Helen Carmichael于2015年加入工作室；她建议他们制作一款以摄政时代为背景的纸牌游戏。“早在2013年，我们就已经在尝试为休闲市场制作游戏。”Birkett表示，“我们最终制作的这类纸牌游戏——市场上已经有一些同类产品，而且已经相当受欢迎——但没有人尝试过Helen提出的这个主题，也就是Regency Solitaire。”

作为摄政时代小说的狂热读者，Carmichael对那个时代上流社会的休闲娱乐活动十分熟悉，主要是赌博和其他室内游戏。她意识到这个时代非常适合作为纸牌游戏的背景设定，而且这对夫妻都是历史爱好者，这更是锦上添花。“Helen读过那些小说，我看过相关电影，我们会去参观庄园和花园等地方，所以做这款游戏对我们来说很有趣，我们也很享受。”Birkett说。

与此同时，Carmichael指出，许多休闲玩家是年长女性，而摄政时代主题的游戏可能对这一受众群体有很大吸引力。随后，她撰写了叙事剧本，将Regency Solitaire中那些在纸牌游戏中非同寻常的元素串联在一起：游戏内商店、装饰品和强化道具。

相关阅读：叙事N

How Forbidden Solitaire brought solitaire games to the forefront
Design
Interviews
How Forbidden Solitaire brought solitaire games to the forefront
Its success has allowed Grey Alien Games to reach out to more Steam players than ever.
Khee Hoon Chan
,
Contributor
August 17, 2026
8 Min Read
Via Gray Alien Games/Night Signal Entertainment
The popularity of
Microsoft Solitaire
—the very salve for bored office workers everywhere—can't be overstated. The staple game that's been pre-installed with Windows since Windows 3.0 in 1990, it has since become synonymous with the genre of solitaire, a family of card games that comes in many variants.
Microsoft Solitaire
, specifically, was based on a version called Klondike. At first glance, solitaire doesn't seem like the sort of card game that's particularly enticing to the average Steam consumer. It's typically a meditative affair, a genre that's more at home within the market of free-to-play casual games than the Steam storefront.
Yet,
Forbidden Solitaire
managed to seize enough attention among these players with its tantalizing, 90s-era analog horror presentation. The game even saw 880 concurrent players at one point since its release in April. In contrast, other solitaire games by developer Grey Alien Games, such as
Regency Solitaire II
and
Shadowhand Solitaire
, only saw 98 and 20 concurrent Steam players at their peak. Moreover,
Forbidden Solitaire
's commercial success—the game
sold 10,000 copies in 48 hours
—meant that Grey Alien Games and its co-developer, Night Signal Entertainment, are able to
consider a sequel
soon after its release. "It's taken awhile to get used to the game's level of success, because we're not used to this game coming out and doing so well," said developer Jake Birkett. "But it has come at the right time, because we did work hard."
Related:
Pushing the limits in Simulating a City, One Page at a Time
Solitaire has become something of a niche for Grey Alien Games, even though Birkett pointed out that it
isn't the only genre
of games they have worked on. "[Forbidden Solitaire] is our seventeenth game by the way," he said. "We made 16 other games, [including] seven match-three games, seven Solitaire games, a city builder [and] some other things." That said, the studio's affinity for solitaire is obvious; it's a genre of games they're good at making.
Most solitaire games are free-to-play casual experiences, with most simply offering straightforward interpretations of the genre. Players clear stacks of cards through repetitive rounds. Not Grey Alien Games' games, however; their creations typically include mechanical variations or wrinkles you may not expect at first glance. Take
Fairway Solitaire
, a game that Birkett worked on as a contractor for Big Fish Games in 2007, which
Kotaku
described as "not just another boring free solitaire game for iPhone;" its solitaire game is mired in golf mechanics. Meanwhile,
Eurogamer
has praised
Regency Solitaire
for its "playful, on-the-nose pastiche of the novels of Jane Austen".
Related:
How Silent Hill: Townfall gets deep into its protagonist's headspace
Then there's Birkett's love for the genre itself, having made his first solitaire game in 1995. While working in a computer shop, he became hooked on
Microsoft Solitaire
, playing it whenever he wasn't building PCs. He then created a version of the game on his Commodore Amiga, even sending it to a publication in hopes that it would be included in the demo discs that were bundled with game magazines at that time. Unfortunately, he never got a response, although that did little to douse his passion for game development. Birkett decided to set up Grey Alien Games, quitting a stable job in business software development in 2005. Subsequently, his wife Helen Carmichael joined the studio in 2015; she suggested that they make a solitaire game set in the Regency era. "We already were trying to make games for the casual market back in 2013," said Birkett. "The type of solitaire games that we ended up making—there were some of those around, and they were already quite popular—but no one had done this theme that Helen came up with, which was
Regency Solitaire
."
A voracious reader of Regency novels, Carmichael was familiar with the leisurely pursuits of the upper class during that era, which are predominantly gambling and other parlor games. She realized that the period would make a suitable setting for a solitaire game, and it didn't hurt that the duo were history buffs. "Helen's read the books, I watched the films, we [would] go and visit stately homes and gardens and things, so it was fun for us to do, and we enjoyed it," said Birkett. At the same time, Carmichael noted that many casual players were older women, and a Regency themed game could have plenty of appeal to this audience. She then wrote the narrative, tying together other elements of Regency Solitaire that were atypical of solitaire games: in-game shops, decorations, and power ups.
Related:
Narrative Notebook #5: UNBEATABLE's music video vibes can't be beat
Finding satisfying twists on a proven formula
These inclusions, in a way, became a blueprint for Grey Alien Games' future solitaire games. Rather than the Klondike variant popularized by
Microsoft Solitaire
,
Regency Solitaire
—and
Forbidden Solitaire
—employed the tri-peaks or golf rulesets instead. "It lends itself to sort of fast, arcade-y gameplay, I would say, where you can build combos and have fun, whereas
Windows Solitaire
is a bit more slow-paced and basic as you build those stacks," he said. To the studio, these seem like a more appealing style of gameplay, akin to a sense of tidying things up. "When you play solitaire, specifically the type in our game, you tidy up, you clear the layout, it's gone," said Birkett. SoulTerra Odyssey
This new soft launch from Bandai Namco appears to be a midcore match 3D roguelite RPG. It was soft-launched August 6 and is currently live only in Australia, New Zealand, the UK, and the Philippines.
Blizzard
Overwatch Rush
This is a top-down, mobile-exclusive hero shooter set in the Overwatch universe that’s in early development. Blizzard says it’ll be announcing testing in selected countries soon, but AppMagic says the iOS edition of the game has already registered over 10k downloads in the Philippines.
EA
Plants vs. Zombies 3: Evolved
PopCap’s merge-based take on the franchise is edging closer to a global release, with Title Update 1.0.5 reworking the new player tutorial and rebalancing rewards ahead of further Early Access rollouts. It’s currently soft launched on iOS and Android in the Philippines, Indonesia, the UK and several other markets.
Farlight
小冰冰斗蛐蛐
This appears to be a midcore auto-battler from Shanghai Lilith’s Farlight label, spun off from the studio’s existing “Xiao Bingbing” IP.
The game is in pre-registration, and it looks like it has soft-launched in China only ahead of a wider October 31 release. No official English title has been announced yet.
Fingersoft
Hill Climb Racing 3
The latest entry in the physics-driven racing series introduces real-time multiplayer for the first time. It has soft launched on Google Play in the UK, Norway, Sweden, and Finland.
Garena
Garena Free City
The Free Fire maker appears to be gearing up to launch a GTA-like game. It first soft-launched on Android in Argentina only, according to
AppMagic
, but it is now registering downloads in the Philippines and Argentina.
Hoyoverse
Petit Planet
Genshin Impact and Honkai: Star Rail maker Mihoyo has opened pre-registration for this cosy life sim, after several rounds of beta tests. There’s no firm release date as yet.
King

今年Gamescom上，谷歌和苹果的参展力度似乎都会更大。尽管这两家平台方在往年都采取不介入的态度，但Games@Google的Tony Clark现表示，Google Play在7号馆的活动是其规模最大的区域消费者推广活动，也是十年来首次大规模亮相Gamescom；而苹果将于8月25日（主展会前一天）在Gamescom Dev举办三场开发者会议。

谷歌的展示内容包含一个奖励中心、一个以Halfbrick的Fruit Ninja为特色的现场竞技场，以及运行Dave the Diver（Mintrocket）、Subway Surfers City（Sybo）、eFootball（Konami）、Wobbly Life（RubberBandGames/Curve Games）和Asphalt Legends（Gameloft）的多游戏体验站。

谷歌还将在8月26日举办一场面向发行商/开发者的“Play After Hours”会议，主题是工作室合作与用户留存。

据苹果的Begüm Ağma Erdal透露，苹果的开发者会议包括：展示苹果面向游戏开发者的硬件/软件；与CD Projekt Red的Paweł Sasko和Jakub Smodrzak一同展示Mac版Cyberpunk 2077；以及与Funday Games的Emil Kjaehr一起探讨如何将游戏带到App Store。

这一友好姿态出现在苹果在其正在进行的Epic Games诉讼案中提议对iOS应用内通过外部链接完成的购买收取新佣金数日之后。具体比例为：标准应用15%，新闻/视频/小程序合作伙伴计划和订阅续费10%，小型企业计划开发者5%。苹果在提交的文件中承认，其在这些交易中的实际成本接近于零。

谷歌也面临着类似压力。

一名法官已命令谷歌降低安装竞争对手Android应用商店的难度，此前Epic的律师展示，在Google Play上搜索“store for apps”时根本没有出现任何第三方商店，而且目前列出的唯一竞争对手商店Aptoide显示的是“查看”按钮，而不是“安装”按钮。

法官称这是“反竞争摩擦”，并给谷歌一周时间修复。

Apple and Google up their Gamescom presence as court dramas continue – Mobilegamer.biz
Skip to content
Both Google and Apple will be more visible at Gamescom this year, it seems.
While both platform holders have been hands-off in prior years,
Games@Google’s Tony Clark has now said
Google Play’s Hall 7 activation is its biggest regional consumer push and first major Gamescom presence in a decade, while Apple is running three developer sessions at Gamescom Dev on August 25, a day before the main show.
Google’s showing includes a rewards hub, a live arena featuring Halfbrick’s Fruit Ninja, and multigaming stations running Dave the Diver (Mintrocket), Subway Surfers City (Sybo), eFootball (Konami), Wobbly Life (RubberBandGames/Curve Games) and Asphalt Legends (Gameloft).
Google is also running a publisher/developer “Play After Hours” session on August 26, on studio partnerships and retention.
Apple’s developer sessions include a showcase of Apple’s hardware/software for game devs, Cyberpunk 2077 on Mac with CD Projekt Red’s Paweł Sasko and Jakub Smodrzak, and bringing games to the App Store with Funday Games’ Emil Kjaehr,
per Apple’s Begüm Ağma Erdal
.
The goodwill comes days after
Apple proposed new commissions on purchases made via external links in iOS apps
, in its ongoing Epic Games case: 15% for standard apps, 10% for News/Video/Mini Apps partner programs and subscription renewals, 5% for Small Business Program developers. Apple’s filing conceded that its actual costs for these transactions are close to zero.
Google is facing similar pressure.
A judge has ordered Google to make it easier to install rival Android app stores
, after Epic’s lawyers showed a search for “store for apps” on Google Play surfaced no third-party stores at all, and that the one rival store currently listed – Aptoide – showed a “View” button rather than “Install.”
The judge called it “anticompetitive friction” and gave Google a week to fix it.

在致Roblox首席执行官David Baszucki的一封信中（via Kotaku），参议员Josh Hawley和Dick Durbin表示，“Roblox上涉嫌的犯罪活动值得国会进行审查。”

“我们不会在这一承诺上妥协。我们期待分享我们如何保护平台上儿童的事实。”

委员会要求Roblox提供近30类文件和资料。其中包括2023年、2024年和2025年收到的“涉及对18岁以下用户的性剥削、诱骗或虐待”的报告数量，Roblox如何回应这些报告，以及这些年有多少账户因这类行为被举报。

委员会还寻求细节：这些指控中有多大比例由人工审查，被举报账户有多大比例被封禁，2023年、2024年和2025年涉及18岁以下用户的欺凌举报数量，以及相关的调查率和封禁率。

“在过去十年中，警方逮捕了多人，他们因通过Roblox结识的儿童实施严重的暴力和伤害行为，包括诱骗、性虐待、绑架、强奸甚至谋杀，”信中继续写道。

委员会还指出，Roblox在2025年向国家失踪与受剥削儿童中心报告了超过65,000起疑似儿童剥削案件，是2024年的两倍多。

“Roblox正被用来交易儿童性虐待材料，参与与儿童相关的色情（且往往暴力的）虚拟‘体验’，贿赂和敲诈儿童制作露骨内容，以及诱骗儿童进行线下见面。这令人心碎。”

“让我们明确一点：你们平台上的儿童正在受伤。国会不会视而不见。”

包括路易斯安那州和洛杉矶县在内的多个美国州和地区已以危害儿童为由起诉Roblox。

澳大利亚政府也提出了类似问题，称这些问题“令许多澳大利亚家长和看护者深感担忧”。

近年来，Roblox增加了各种新的安全措施。这些措施包括阻止13岁以下用户使用直接消息的功能、全球面部识别检查、为其“体验”功能添加“敏感问题”内容标签，以及更强有力的审核政策和行动。

如果你点击链接并购买商品，我们可能会获得少量佣金。
请阅读我们的编辑政策。
你可能还记得《Join Us》的预告片在六月份的Xbox Showcase上展出过。它描绘了一款黑暗幽默的合作邪教模拟游戏，身着长袍的邪教成员骑着猪，发射机枪，最后以克苏鲁风格的巨型触手画面收尾。但开发者Wolf Haus Games的首席执行官兼创意总监Joe Dietsch表示，预告片中没有展示蛇枪。
Joe Dietsch |
图片来源：
Wolf Haus Games
“我们一位团队成员的儿子想出了这个点子，”他回忆道。“他们说，‘能不能有一把蛇枪？’我们有一个工具可以快速缩放制作枪支，所以大约半小时内，我就进去做了一把能射出蛇的枪。那对他来说太震撼了。它现在还在游戏里。”
这个故事体现了《Join Us》中预期会出现的混乱玩法，这是一款开放世界沙盒生存游戏，玩家可以招募追随者——或合作玩家——加入他们70年代风格的邪教。这也体现了团队以技术为核心的方法，这使他们能够用相对极少的开发人员制作出一款大型高保真游戏。Wolf Haus的首席运营官Michael Abbott表示，“我们想成为颠覆者”。
“我们当时说，‘看，我们不需要一百个人，我们十二个人就能搞定一切’。而每个人都说那不可能，他们就是不相信我们。”然而，团队在预算有限的情况下完成大事方面已有经验。“我们来自独立电影行业，习惯了超越自身能力去拼搏。”团队进行了80次推介，最终才从Krafton和Lifelike Capital获得了资金，两家公司均获得了Wolf Haus的股权。
家族渊源
Wolf Haus背后的创始团队有着深厚的好莱坞背景。Dietsch在加州查普曼大学学习电影，与Mel Gibson的儿子Louie Gibson（也是Wolf Haus的联合创始人）一起，两人联合编剧并联合执导了电影《Happy Hunting》和《Manifest West》。与此同时，Abbott是好莱坞化妆师Larry Abbott的儿子，曾协助创办了Ascendant Pictures——这家电影制作公司由Chris Roberts在转向《Star Citizen》之前创立。Abbott后来担任了由Jamie Foxx主演的《Fight for '84》等电影的制作人。
Michael Abbott |
图片来源：
Wolf Haus Games
《Join Us》起源于Dietsch在虚幻引擎中随意摆弄。“这是一个非常简单的开端，就是我发现虚幻引擎可以免费下载，”他解释道。“我热爱游戏多年，我看电影的时间和我玩游戏的时间一样长，但感觉在那个领域真正创作东西有极高的门槛。但我拿起了虚幻引擎，开始探索它能实现什么，只是通过YouTube教程学习。”

他开始制作概念验证。“在我心里，有点像，‘我要尽可能把它推进下去’，我假设在某个时候我会撞到墙——在某个时候会出现技术挑战，让我觉得，‘好吧，这就是为什么我不该做这个’。”他把演示给Abbott看。“然后Michael把它带给了Dooma。”

You might recall the trailer for Join Us being featured in the Xbox Showcase back in June. It depicts a darkly comic co-op cult simulator, with robed cult members riding around on pigs and loosing off machine guns, before ending on an image of Cthulu-like giant tentacles. Not shown was the snake gun, says Joe Dietsch, CEO and creative director of Join Us developer Wolf Haus Games.
Joe Dietsch  |
Image credit:
Wolf Haus Games
"One of our team member's sons had come up with the idea," he recalls. "They said, 'Can there be a snake gun?' And we had a tool to make a gun that can be very quickly scaled, so in half an hour or something, I went in and made a gun that shoots snakes. That was mind-blowing for him. It's still in the game."
The story is indicative of the kind of chaotic gameplay to expect in Join Us, an open-world sandbox survival title in which the player can recruit followers – or co-op players – to their 70s-style cult. It's also indicative of the team's tech-focused approach, which has allowed them to make a big, high-fidelity game with a relatively tiny number of developers. Michael Abbott, COO of Wolf Haus, says that "we wanted to be disruptors".
"We were saying, 'Look, we don't need a hundred people, we could do everything with twelve'. And everybody just said that's impossible, they just wouldn't believe us." Yet the team has had experience of doing big things on small budgets. "We come from indie films, and we're used to really punching above our weight." The team did 80 pitches before finally securing funding from Krafton and Lifelike Capital, both of which took an equity stake in Wolf Haus.
Family ties
The founding team behind Wolf Haus has deep Hollywood roots. Dietsch studied film at California's Chapman University alongside Mel Gibson's son Louie Gibson – another Wolf Haus co-founder – and the pair co-wrote and co-directed the movies Happy Hunting and Manifest West. Abbott, meanwhile, is the son of Hollywood make-up artist Larry Abbott, and helped to set up Ascendant Pictures – the film production company founded by Chris Roberts before he moved on to Star Citizen. Abbott would later work as a producer on films like Fight for '84, starring Jamie Foxx.
Michael Abbott  |
Image credit:
Wolf Haus Games
Join Us originated from Dietsch fooling around in Unreal. "It's a very simple beginning, which is that I found that Unreal Engine was free to download," he explains. "I'd loved games for years, I've played games as long as I've watched movies, but it felt like there was this extreme barrier to entry to actually create something in that space. But I picked up Unreal Engine and started exploring what was possible with it, just learning from YouTube tutorials."
Despite having no previous experience, Dietsch managed to create a couple of small games, before deciding to try something bigger. "I kept coming back to this idea of a doomsday cult simulator, because it combined a lot of things I like with survival and grindhouse cinema, bridging things I like in movies and games into one IP."
He began work on a proof of concept. "In my mind, it was sort of like, 'I'll take this as far as I can go', and I assumed at some point I would hit the wall – at some point there would be this tech challenge where it's like, 'Okay, that's why I'm not supposed to do this'." He showed the demo to Abbott. "And Michael then took it to Dooma."

Dooma Wendschuh, chief financial officer and narrative director at Wolf Haus, began his career as a producer and a screenwriter in the film industry, but moved into video games in the early 2000s by setting up Sekretagent Productions, which provided writing services for Prince of Persia: The Two Thrones, Assassin's Creed, and Batman: Arkham Origins. He went on to found several tech firms in the 2010s, including the cannabis formulation company Ebbu, which was later sold for C$430 million ($330 million).
Then he bought a restaurant on a tiny island in the middle of nowhere in Canada, and "figured I was just retired and would go to the beach and walk my dog," he says. But in the best Hollywood tradition, just when he thought he was out, they pulled him back in.
Dooma Wendschuh  |
Image credit:
Wolf Haus Games
"I got a call out of the blue from my old roommate back in the Hollywood Hills, Michael Abbott. And he said, 'A buddy of mine has made a video game'. I get a lot of calls like that. As a courtesy to my old roommate, I took that call and looked at the video game that Joe had made. And it just blew my mind – and got me out of retirement." Wendschuh took the game to Reid Schneider, a former VP at Warner Bros Games and now head of Journey to the Savage Planet maker Raccoon Logic. Schneider joined as a strategic advisor and recruited Pierre-Olivier Chartrand, previously a programmer at Ubisoft Montreal, as chief technology officer.
The team was taking shape; the next step was funding, which proved a lot harder. The team started pitching in the summer of 2023, with the industry downturn well advanced. "People would always see the game we were building and say, 'Oh, this is cool', but it was a challenging time," says Dietsch. "So we did initial outreach, and then subsequently signed with our agents, CAA [Creative Artists Agency] in Los Angeles, and regrouped with them, and went back out for pitches in 2024. And we eventually secured our seed round with Lifelike Capital and Krafton."
The game is a co-op survival title, slated to release next year. |

标题：为游戏行业巨额交易提供建议的人 — Deconstructor of Fun
0
为游戏行业巨额交易提供建议的人
商业
投资/并购
8月17日
撰写人
Aylin Yazıcı

Affan Butt联合创立了Aream & Co.，这家投资银行迄今已为超过110笔游戏交易提供顾问服务，交易总额高达惊人的400亿美元。Affan一直坐在创始人一边，代表他们与各种买家谈判。所以我问他，在今天的环境下，创始人在出售公司之前应该知道些什么。

在Deconstructor of Fun收听完整对话

Affan Butt正沿着伦敦的Regent Street行走，身旁是Akin Babaygit，后者正在谈论来自伊斯坦布尔的最新火箭式增长公司。惊人的数据，正在融资。Affan问他们为什么选择融资而不是出售。理由很简单：在混合休闲游戏领域，没人能预见未来，而如果规模足够大，最终你反正会卖给沙特人或中国人。那为什么不趁现在图表还在垂直上升时，就带着结构性地展开这场对话？

这家公司是Loom Games。创立四个月，员工不到十人，一款前景看好但没人能预测六个月后走势的游戏。Affan的公司将其出售给了沙特所有的Scopely，交易金额超过十亿美元。

这家公司就是Aream & Co.，由他与Kartik Parbhakara于2019年共同创立。七年间完成超过110笔交易，交易总额达400亿美元，过去五年游戏行业所有1亿美元以上卖方交易中，超过一半由他们经手。他坐在创始人一边，代表他们与各种买家谈判。所以我问他，在今天的环境下，创始人在出售公司之前应该知道些什么。

交易在交易开始前数年就已萌芽

成功的秘诀在于，你大多数时候只需要被人喜欢。

“2012年，我在LinkedIn上联系了Ilkka Paananen（Supercell的CEO兼联合创始人）。我说，嘿，我只是想来坐坐聊聊。不知为何，他说‘好啊’。”

Affan飞往赫尔辛基，几乎花了一整天时间和Ilkka及Petteri待在一起——后者当时是Supercell的董事会主席，如今是传奇风险投资人。他没有推销任何东西。当时Hay Day刚刚上线，Clash还未问世，Sensor Tower也还不存在，没有什么数据可以拿来卖弄聪明。

同样的模式也发生在伊斯坦布尔。2012年他出现在Sidar（Peak创始人）的办公室时，那里只有四个人。那些行程中有很多都毫无结果。他说，如果十年前就能知道哪些公司会成为独角兽，他会去做投资而不是做顾问。

幕布之后

中间发生的事情归结为准备和心理。

正式的并购流程从首次接触到交割大约需要六个月。但正是关系层面的工作才可能让正式流程花费数年时间，而且这些工作在计时开始之前就已经进行了。这也是为什么Affan对创始人主动找上门的企业发展部门兴趣持怀疑态度。创始人往往把大公司发来的热情洋溢的邮件当作对自己的认可，而实际上，那只是企业发展专业人士工作职责的一部分。

关于准备，他讲了一个隐去名字的故事。他们做了推介，就估值、买家名单、时间表和费用达成一致，并签了约。一周后，在尽职调查启动会议上，创始人把自己的预测下调了百分之二十五。信任就此丧失，交易也崩了。

当FOMO适得其反时

今天的收购方池子也比过去更小，这就是为什么竞购战可能适得其反。

关于FOMO（错失恐惧），他拒绝接受那种奉承式的回答。“我们当然希望认为我们（银行家）是魔术师，但现实是，是游戏和团队本身创造了真正的FOMO。”银行家增加的价值是让事情具有可执行性的可信度。

今天的收购方池子也比过去更小，而且不是出于商业原因。地缘政治在讨论价格之前就排除了买家，通常没有任何正式的裁决文件。大家就是心照不宣。

创始人最难相信的一点是：在Loom的交易中，第一天就有更好的报价。但创始人还是选择了Scopely。“如果有人说，‘这是一亿美元，很多钱，比六千万多。就算不行，谁在乎呢？我有一亿了。’但事情不是那样的。对于创始人来说，那是他们的公司，是他们的孩子。”

这就是为什么竞购战可能适得其反。在告诉一个买家你正在进行一场低调的流程之后，又把推介材料群发给每一个有邮箱地址的人——这就是一个小型行业不再信任你的方式。代价会落在签约到交割之间那三个月里，那期间总会有事情出岔子。

“如果你表现得纯粹交易导向，你唯一关心的就是最后一分钱，那么当任何事出了岔子时，买家就会说，‘实际上，我想要回一部分钱。’而另一种情况是，我们说好了签了约，别担心，我们一起解决。每个人都同样满意或同样不满意，才是正确的交易。”

与直觉相反的是，Affan也经常告诉创始人不要出售，频率比你想象的要高，通常是因为他了解买家那边的情况。

Affan Butt
was walking down London’s Regent Street with
Akin Babaygit
, who was talking about the latest rocket ship out of Istanbul. Astonishing metrics, raising money. Affan asked why they were raising instead of selling. The argument was simple: nobody can see around the corner in hybridcasual, and if it gets big enough, you end up selling to the Saudis or the Chinese anyway. So why not have that conversation now, with structure, while the chart is still vertical?
The company was
Loom Games
. Four months old, fewer than a dozen people, one promising game nobody could forecast six months out. Affan's firm sold it to Saudi-owned
Scopely
for over a billion dollars.
That firm is Aream & Co, which he set up in 2019 with
Kartik Parbhakara
. Over 110 transactions in seven years, $40 billion in value, more than half of all $100M-plus sell-side deals in gaming over the last five years. He sits on the founder’s side of the table and negotiates with every kind of buyer on their behalf. So I asked him what a founder should know before selling today.
HOW DEALS START YEARS BEFORE THE DEAL
The secret to being successful is that you mostly just have to be liked.
"In 2012, I reached out to
Ilkka Paananen
(CEO and co-founder of Supercell) on LinkedIn. I said, hey, I just want to come hang out. And for some reason, he said Sure."
Affan flew to Helsinki and spent almost the entire day with Ilkka and Petteri, then Supercell's president of the board and a legendary venture capitalist today. He pitched nothing. Hay Day had just launched, Clash was still coming, and
Sensor Tower
did not exist yet, so there was no data to be clever with.
Same pattern in Istanbul, where he showed up at the Sidar's (founder of Peak) office in 2012 when there were four people in it. Plenty of those trips went nowhere. If he knew ten years out who the unicorns would be, he says, he would be investing instead of advising.
BEHIND THE CURTAIN
What happens in between comes down to preparation and psychology.
The formal M&A process runs roughly six months from first outreach to close. Yet it’s the relationship work that makes the formal process possibly take years and happens before the clock starts. This is also why Affan treats inbound corporate development interest from founders with suspicion. Founders tend to read a warm email from a big company as validation when it’s, in reality, part of a corporate development professional’s job description.
On preparation, he told a story with the name removed. They pitched, agreed on valuation, buyer list, timeline, and fees, and signed. One week later, at the due diligence kickoff meeting, the founders lowered their own projections by twenty-five percent. The trust was lost, and the deal crashed.

The pool of acquirers is also smaller today than it used to be, which is why a bidding war can backfire.
On FOMO, he refused the flattering answer. "We would love to think we (bankers) are magicians, but the reality is that it is the game and the team that creates the real FOMO." What the banker adds is credibility that something is actionable.
The pool of acquirers is also smaller today than it used to be, and not for commercial reasons. Geopolitics removes buyers before price is ever discussed, usually with no formal ruling anywhere. It is just understood.
The part founders find hardest to believe: on Loom, there were better offers on day one. The founders took Scopely anyway. "If somebody says, ' Here is a hundred million bucks, that is a lot of money, and it is more than sixty. If it does not work out, who cares? I have a hundred million. But that is not how it works. For founders, it is their company. It is their baby."
Which is why a bidding war can backfire. Blasting a teaser to everyone with an email account after telling a buyer you were running a quiet process is how a small industry stops trusting you. The cost lands in the three-month gap between signing and closing, when something always goes sideways.
"If you have come across as transactional, and the only thing you cared about was the last penny, then when anything goes sideways, the buyer says, ' Actually, I want some of that money back. Versus saying, we signed a deal, do not worry; let us sort this out together. Everybody equally happy or equally unhappy is the right deal."
Counterintuitively, Affan also tells founders not to sell more often than you would expect, usually because he knows the buyer landscape has no market for that profile right now. Some founders take another opinion from another banker and hit the market anyway. His argument is that no one is free.
"Why do you want to get twenty no’s when I have high conviction it is going to be a no? It goes in the acquirers’ database. They looked at it and said no. Next time, the bar is just much higher."
SELL, SOME, AND KEEP BUILDING
The most expensive mistake is not a bad deal. It is a missed one.
"The vast majority of regrets are the ones that did not happen. Theoretically, tomorrow you are always going to be more valuable than today. But that is theoretical, and that is on Excel, and that is in a world where nothing is changing."

articles.translated_content:
标题：Saber Interactive 为 Steam 上的 Rideshare 添加 AI 声明；CEO 向前主编剧道歉

正文：
Saber Interactive 为 Steam 上的 Rideshare Simulator 页面添加了 AI 声明，此前该公司被指控解雇了一名参与该游戏开发的编剧，转而使用 AI 撰写的文案，此事引发了争议。

以下是声明全文：
“主线战役故事、角色和对话由一支人类编剧团队撰写。AI 工具仅用于语音生成和部分本地化。

可选的 Free Ride 模式包含 AI 生成的乘客任务和本地化对话。Free Ride 模式与主线战役相互独立，偏好仅体验人类撰写叙事内容的玩家可以跳过该模式。

游戏还包含一系列混合电台，其中既有真人创作的音乐，也有 AI 生成的音乐。包含 AI 生成音乐的电台在游戏中均有明确标注。”

此次更新之前，Saber CEO Matt Karch 曾就编剧 Stella Sacco 一事发表评论。Sacco 于 2023 年 7 月至 2024 年 7 月期间在 Saber 工作，她表示自己在 Rideshare 开发中途被移除，并由 ChatGPT 取代，同时她还指控游戏开发过程中存在其他当时尚未公开的 AI 使用情况。

对此，Karch 回应称，Sacco“被一位更有才华的人取代，并在几个月后因多种原因被解雇”，并补充道“事后看来，[他] 很乐意用 AI 取代她”。

“Stella 是谁？我不得不去问 Claude，因为我从未和她说过话，也从未见过她，”Karch 告诉 This Week In Videogames。“我们已经说过会在游戏的某些部分使用 AI，一旦我们确定了功能集，就会更新 Steam 页面。”

“我们认为在这款特定游戏中使用 AI——这将是一款定价较低的作品——对消费者来说是一个加分项。”

在本周末的一篇 BlueSky 帖子中，Sacco 写道，Karch“毫无保留地为他媒体上谈论我的糟糕方式道了歉。”

“我从一开始就坚持说我说的都是实话；我想现在我们都同意这一点已经得到了证实。Matt 表示希望弥补我的损失；目前我还不太清楚这对我来说意味着什么，我需要一些时间来慢慢消化，但我至少接受了他的道歉。”

Karch 另外在 LinkedIn 上公开发表了一份声明。“不幸的是，我被后来的一些评论激怒了（出于我不会深入讨论的原因），我不假思索地选择了先发制人的回应方式，”他写道。“这种事时有发生，我也是人。我已经尽我所能去纠正了。”

Saber Interactive has added an AI disclaimer to Rideshare Simulator's
Steam page
following controversy over allegations the firm had dismissed a writer working on the game in favour of using AI-written copy.
Here's the disclosure in full:
The main campaign story, characters, and dialogue are written by a team of human writers. AI tools are used for voice generation and some localisation.
The optional Free Ride mode includes AI-generated passenger missions and localised dialogue. Free Ride mode is separate from the main campaign and can be skipped by players who prefer to experience only human-written narrative content.
The game also includes a mix of radio stations featuring human-made music and AI-generated music. Stations containing AI-generated music are clearly labeled as such in game."
This update follows
comments from Saber CEO Matt Karch
regarding writer Stella Sacco, who worked at Saber from July 2023 to July 2024, and stated she was removed from Rideshare midway through development and replaced with ChatGPT, while alleging other then-unannounced use of AI in the game's development.
In response, Karch stated that Sacco was "replaced by someone more talented and terminated for a variety of reasons a few months later," and added that "in retrospect [he] would have been happy to replace her with AI."
"Stella who? I had to ask Claude because I have never spoken to her or seen her," Karch told
This Week In Videogames
. "We have already said we are using AI for certain parts of the game and will update the Steam page once we have finalised the feature set."
"We look at our use of AI in this particular game, which will be a lower priced title, as a plus for consumers."
In a
BlueSky
post this weekend Sacco wrote that Karch had "apologised unreservedly for the awful way he spoke about me in the press."
"I've been firm from the beginning that I was telling the truth; I think we can all now agree that it's been borne out. Matt expressed a desire to make it right with me; at this time I don't really know what that looks like for me, and I'll have to take some time to sit with it, but I do at least accept his apology."
Karch separately posted a public comment on
LinkedIn
. "I unfortunately got triggered by certain later comments (for reasons I won't get into) and shot first and thought second about how to respond," he wrote. "It happens and I am a human being. I have done what I can to rectify."
